inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 diluted weighted-average (10-Q, WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding 828,875,000 incl. 3,678,000 dilutive share-based awards), post 15-for-1 split of 2025-06-10. The Metrics.csv SharesOutstanding column is this diluted series and is now continuous on the post-split basis for every period (FY2008-Q1 2024 rows were rescaled x15 on 2026-10-02 via make fix, recorded in ORLY_Corrections.jsonl; the Q2-2026 figure was already post-split and is unchanged). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Buybacks (TTM $3,353M) are the mechanism that keeps the count flat and then some; the model gives no credit for the net shrink beyond that.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow-statement share-based compensation add-back, TTM to 2026-06-30 (FY2025 35.115 + H1-2026 17.512 - H1-2025 18.812). ORLY publishes no combined equity-award figure and tags no net-share-settlement tax withholding (awards are predominantly options, exercise proceeds are an inflow), so sbc_incl_equity_taxes equals the add-back.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM repurchases to 2026-06-30 (FY2025 2,096.96 + H1-2026 2,433.02 - H1-2025 1,176.64). Actual financing outflow, not the $31.75B cumulative authorization. H1-2026 repurchases exceeded FCF by ~$0.95B, funded by the $0.82B Q2 debt increase.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity 4.2% 10y UST + 0.75 beta x 5.0% ERP = 7.95% (ORLY's observed beta is 0.6-0.9; defensive aftermarket demand). Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (recent senior notes 4.7-5.1%), 3.85% after 23% tax. Market weights ~91% equity / 9% debt (equity ~$70.5B at the quoted price, debt $7.0B) -> 7.6%, rounded to 7.5%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariff margin volatility and NAPA deal risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. ASC 842 operating leases: the full lease payment ($453.5M FY2025, $235.2M H1-2026) is a single straight-line cost inside SG&A, so reported EBITDA (operating income + D&A) is already post-lease and OCF already carries the cash. Lease liabilities ($2,572.9M at 2026-06-30: 452.3 current + 2,120.6 non-current) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A ($537.7M TTM) is PP&E-only -- ROU amortisation is inside the lease cost line -- so cash-tax EBIT does not charge the lease twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: no non-controlling interests; all subsidiaries wholly owned.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (capex is normalising from a record 7.0% of revenue toward ~5.5% while D&A catches up, so the owner-FCF margin is still moving at year 5). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 1-2: wholly-owned US specialty retailer, cash flows mean what the engine assumes. Not a REIT/bank/holdco; the NEGATIVE shareholders' equity (-$1,835.7M at 2026-06-30) is the product of $31B+ of cumulative buybacks shrinking the count ~57% since 2011, not distress -- book-value-based metrics and the equity CAGR are meaningless here and are not used. ANCHORS: price is the 2026-10-01 regular close; balance sheet, debt, lease liabilities and diluted shares are all from the Q2-2026 10-Q (2026-06-30). total_debt is LongTermDebtNoncurrent only -- no current portion is tagged at 2026-06-30, so there is no current-portion double count (the Q2 jump from $6,195M to $7,015M funded Q2 buybacks of ~$1.5B against Q2 FCF of ~$0.7B). FY0 is the trailing twelve months to the same date so flows, bridge and divisor share one vintage; Y1 is therefore Jul-2026 to Jun-2027 and is discounted a full year (end-of-year convention), which is slightly conservative given the valuation date is already a quarter into that year. EBITDA margin driver is the SBC-inclusive adjusted figure (reported EBITDA 22.45% + SBC 0.18% = 22.63%) because the engine subtracts the SBC path from it. Cash tax at 23% throughout: FY2025 cash taxes paid ($1,067.5M) ran above the ~22.8% book provision while FY2023 ($315.1M) ran well below, so the three-year average (~21% of EBIT) is noise around a 21% federal + state rate; no NOL or credit distorts it. Working capital: ORLY's supplier-financing programme keeps payables above inventory, so growth has historically released cash (FY2022 +55% of the revenue increase, FY2023 +18%, FY2024 +19%) but FY2025 consumed cash (-30%) on inventory build and tariff-inflated cost; base captures 5% of the revenue change, bull 10%, bear -5%. Interest income is immaterial (net debt, cash $262M) and not stripped. No equity bridge items: lease liabilities are excluded by the lease treatment, there are no non-operating assets or investments of note, and the reported ~$10B NAPA bid is unconfirmed and left out of all scenarios except as a risk weight. Split: 15-for-1 on 2025-06-10. The Metrics.csv share-count and EPS history was corrected to a continuous post-split basis on 2026-10-02 (76 periods: shares x15, EPS /15, plus one mistagged Q3-2024 EPS cell); the per-share CAGRs below are read straight off the corrected CSV and equal the hand-adjusted figures of the first build, so no driver or anchor moved.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case Y1-Y3 average (5.5/6.0/5.5), anchored to the FY2026 guide (revenue $18.9-19.2B, comps 4-6%, 225-235 new stores) and the long-run algorithm of 3-5% comps plus ~3% unit growth. The equity CAGR -- the house default anchor -- is undefined because book equity is negative at both ends of every window; the revenue 3yr CAGR (7.3%) is the upper reference and the owner-FCF CAGR is negative for the reason in the notes.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR cannot be computed (shareholders' equity -$1,060.8M FY2022, -$763.4M FY2025, -$1,835.7M Q2-2026; negative by design from buybacks). Owner-FCF CAGR (-15.2% 3yr, -7.9% 5yr) diverges from revenue (+7.3%/+8.9%) and EPS (+9.8%/+13.5%) because capex stepped from 3.3-3.9% of revenue in FY2021-22 (COVID-depressed) to 6.1-6.6% in FY2023-25 (record store openings, DC programme, Mexico) and FY2025 working capital consumed $0.3B; the TTM to Jun-2026 owner FCF ($2,122M) has already recovered above FY2022 (-$2,558M) on an H1-2026 working-capital release. SBC is 0.18% of revenue, so the owner/reported FCF gap is immaterial.
historical_growth.notes: Windows: 3yr = FY2022->FY2025, 5yr = FY2020->FY2025, annual XBRL rows. EPS from the split-corrected CSV (FY2020 1.583, FY2022 2.250, FY2025 2.98; identical to the first build's hand-adjusted values, so the 2026-10-02 split fix changed no CAGR). Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (no interest income or equity-award tax lines): FY2020 2,348.3, FY2022 2,558.5, FY2025 1,558.1.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 5.5% = H2-2026 at the guidance midpoint (+5.2% on H2-2025) plus ~6% for H1-2027; Y2 6.0% carries the record 2026-27 store cohort; then decays 0.5pp/yr toward 3% as the US footprint saturates and comps revert to the 3-4% aging-fleet trend.
base.margin_rationale: 22.6% is the TTM SBC-inclusive EBITDA margin (operating margin 19.6% + D&A 2.9% + SBC 0.2%). +40bp over five years from professional-channel density and DC leverage; FY2026 operating-margin guide of 19.3-19.8% is consistent with the first two years. Operating margin has sat in 19.3-20.8% for a decade bar FY2021's 21.9%, so no return to that peak is assumed.
base.capex_rationale: 7.0% = FY2026 guide of $1.3-1.4B on $19.05B (record 225-235 US stores, DC expansion, Mexico/Canada). Normalises to 5.5% by Y8, in line with FY2018-19 (5.3-6.2%) and above the FY2021-22 COVID trough of 3.3-3.9%. D&A follows capex up from 2.9% to 3.4%; the terminal 2.1pp capex-over-D&A gap funds 3% unit-plus-inventory growth.

scenario_narratives.base: The dual-market algorithm keeps working: comps settle at 3-5% on an aging US fleet (average vehicle age at record highs), the record 2026 store cohort and a ~3%/yr unit cadence carry revenue growth from 5.5-6% toward 3%, and professional-channel density adds ~40bp of EBITDA margin over five years. Capex normalises from the 7% peak to 5.5% as the DC build-out and the Mexico/Canada entry mature, working capital gives a small supplier-financing tailwind, and the cash tax rate stays ~23%. Buybacks continue at roughly free cash flow, which in this model is value-neutral (flat count, SBC expensed). The reported NAPA bid is excluded: unconfirmed, and a $10B debt-funded deal would belong in its own scenario if announced.
scenario_narratives.bull: Professional share gains continue at the Q2-2026 pace (four straight double-digit pro comps) as independents and Advance Auto Parts cede ground, taking revenue growth to 7-7.5% for three years; the denser delivery network and purchasing scale lift the EBITDA margin to 24.5% -- above every year since FY2021's 21.9% operating margin -- while capex settles at 5.2% once the DC programme is complete. Supplier financing captures 10% of revenue growth as cash and terminal growth is 3%. The bull case requires both the growth and the margin legs; a NAPA deal on good terms would be upside to it but is not modelled.
scenario_narratives.bear: Tariff-driven cost volatility, AutoZone's and Amazon's pricing, and a softer DIY consumer compress comps to 2-3% and the EBITDA margin by ~2pp to 20.5% (operating margin ~17%, below any year since FY2013). Store growth continues but the new cohort ramps slowly, so capex stays elevated at 6% against low growth; supplier financing goes into reverse as the AP/inventory ratio compresses, consuming 5% of the revenue increase. Terminal growth 2% and a 16x cap reflect a business re-rated from compounder to mature retailer. Leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~1.6x ex-leases, ~2.2x with leases) is not a solvency issue at this margin, so the bear is a de-rating and growth story, not a going-concern one; a debt-funded NAPA acquisition that stalls on antitrust or integration would deepen it.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 20% because two live two-sided risks sit outside the base path -- the unconfirmed ~$10B NAPA bid (antitrust, integration and a debt-funded balance sheet already at -$1.8B book equity) and tariff-timing margin volatility that management itself calls 'choppy'. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs two independent things to hold for a decade -- sustained high-single-digit pro share gains AND a margin level never reached in the company's history outside the FY2021 stimulus year. No going-concern or covenant pressure, so bear is not pushed higher.

reconciliation.note: Same-day rebuild after the Metrics.csv 15-for-1 split correction (76 pre-FY2023 share-count/EPS cells). The fix touched historical per-share data only; the FY0 anchor (TTM to 2026-06-30), Q2-2026 net debt and diluted share count were already post-split, and every CAGR recomputes to the value the first build had already hand-adjusted. No driver path, weight or anchor was changed; the Drivers edits are prose describing the CSV basis.

bridge.item: Anchor refresh (price, net debt, shares): none, same vintage
Driver changes: none (split fix altered historical EPS/share rows only)

valuation_philosophy.summary: ORLY is valued as a stream of owner free cash flow from a wholly-owned, defensive specialty retailer: reported FCF less SBC, built bottom-up from revenue, an SBC-inclusive EBITDA margin that already carries ASC 842 lease cost, D&A, a 23% cash tax rate, capex that normalises from a record investment year, and a supplier-financing working-capital capture on the change in revenue. Leases are treated once (in the flows, excluded from net debt); SBC is charged once (expensed, count flat); the three scenarios share one 7.5% USD WACC with risk carried in the flows and the weights. The valuation gives no credit to the buyback programme beyond keeping the count flat, which is the right accounting for a repurchaser paying ~26x earnings for its own stock, and none to the NAPA bid. The headline test is simply whether a 7.5% required return on these flows supports today's price; the required-return table shows what return the market price actually implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value dominates (10-year explicit build at a 2.5-3% perpetuity / 16-20x cap); a 1pp move in WACC or 0.5pp in terminal growth is worth more than any single driver-year.
Capex normalisation path (7.0% -> 5.5%) is a judgment, not guidance; if the DC and international programme keeps capex at 6.5%+ indefinitely the owner-FCF margin stays ~1pp lower.
Working-capital capture assumes the supplier-financing programme stays at ~125-130% AP/inventory; FY2025 showed it can reverse ($0.3B consumed) and a tariff-inflated inventory cost makes it noisy.
A confirmed ~$10B NAPA acquisition would re-cut the model entirely: a different asset base, synergy case, integration risk and leverage; it is deliberately excluded here rather than half-modelled.

FY0 is a TTM anchored to a June balance sheet valued in October; Q3-2026 results (late October) will move the anchor -- the FY2026 guide was raised at Q2 and a further raise or a cut both land directly in Y1.
Negative book equity means P/B, ROE and the equity CAGR are undefined -- any sanity check built on book value will misfire and should be read as such, not as a signal.
